note: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts predicted vemurafenib's pathway blockade, exposure threshold, tumour regression and the V600E-only patient rule; rat/dog toxicology was silent on the cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas that the RAS-mutant paradoxical-activation model first explained (2010) and then predicted prospectively (RAS genotypes, MEK co-inhibition).
label: Melanoma (BRAF)

engagement.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
engagement.note: PLX4720 blocked ERK phosphorylation only in BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts; no patient biopsy comparison yet.
engagement.short: pERK blocked only in V600E cells
engagement.quote: Consistent with the high degree of selectivity, ERK phosphorylation is potently inhibited by PLX4720 in B-Raf(V600E)-bearing tumor cell lines but not in cells lacking oncogenic B-Raf.
engagement.judgement: Strip opener. PLX4720 is the tool analogue, not a member drug, so product_in_model is false; the vemurafenib product repeated the pERK/pMEK blockade in V600E lines (Yang 2010, doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-10-0646) and the FDA pharmacology review names the xenograft pMEK/pERK studies, so model_filed is true.

engagement.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
engagement.note: Paired phase-1 biopsies: >80% tumour pERK inhibition, the broad blockade xenografts needed for regression, correlated with clinical response.
engagement.quote: At higher drug exposures afforded by a new amorphous drug formulation, greater than 80% inhibition of ERK phosphorylation in the tumours of patients correlated with clinical response.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract verbatim (British spelling); full text read via the PMC author manuscript PMC2948082.
engagement.reason: Patient biopsies matched xenograft pERK blockade
engagement.judgement: One paper (Plexxikon/Roche authors) holds both sides: xenograft pathway blockade and regression versus pre/day-15 patient biopsies from NCT00405587 (PLX06-02; results first posted 2017-08-22). Readout is pERK, two steps below the target (BRAF's own product is pMEK), so readout_tier is downstream. The xenograft side gives no numeric pERK threshold, so magnitude is direction_only.
engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour pERK inhibition; xenograft side reported as pathway blockade without a numeric threshold

dose.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
dose.note: Oral PLX4720 regressed V600E xenografts without toxicity; the exposure titration that set the clinical AUC target came with PLX4032 (Bollag 2010).
dose.quote: In B-Raf(V600E)-dependent tumor xenograft models, orally dosed PLX4720 causes significant tumor growth delays, including tumor regressions, without evidence of toxicity.
dose.judgement: Strip opener on the tool analogue; the Colo205 AUC titration itself is in Bollag 2010.

dose.note: Colo205 xenografts regressed only at AUC0-24 ~300 uM.h; patients below 300 uM.h had no tumour shrinkage, those above did, and the 960 mg BID MTD sat far above.
dose.short: Patient regressions began above xenograft AUC
dose.quote: Patients exposed to plasma levels of PLX4032 less than 300 μM·h experienced no measurable decreases in tumor burden.
dose.confidence_note: Quote from the PMC author manuscript (PMC2948082); model side in the same text: 'significant tumor regressions were observed at 20 mg/kg BID (AUC0-24 ~ 300 μM*hr)'.
dose.judgement: Target reached and the drug worked: same. Margin: the paper states toxicology 'confirmed a wide safety margin' and no skin histology change in rat or dog, and patients were dosed to 960 mg BID (AUC0-24 1741 uM.h) with DLTs only at 1120 mg, so margin_stated is true; the harm the margin did not foresee (cuSCC) is counted once, in safety. Model and patient thresholds are both ~300 uM.h, so within_2x.
dose.magnitude_basis: AUC0-24 threshold for tumour regression: ~300 uM.h in Colo205 xenografts vs >300 uM.h in phase-1 patients

dose.note: FDA restated the comparison: first patient regressions at 240-360 mg BID, the cohorts that crossed the xenograft-derived 400 uM.h threshold.
dose.short: FDA: regressions once xenograft AUC crossed
dose.quote: Consistent with nonclinical findings, tumor regressions in PLX06-02 were first observed in the dose range of 240 mg b.i.d. to 360 mg b.i.d. that on average exceeded the target exposure threshold AUC0-24h of 400 µM*hr.
dose.confidence_note: Pharmacology review p.105, 'Correlation with Clinical Toxicity', NDA 202429, signed 2011-07-27/28.
dose.reason: Xenograft AUC threshold held in patients
dose.judgement: Regulator-stated version of the 2010 comparison, kept as a strengthening entry rather than a status change. The review attributes the >400 uM.h threshold to 'xenograft models' generally (sponsor interpretation) and does not name Colo205.
dose.magnitude_basis: AUC0-24 regression threshold 400 uM.h (xenograft) vs the 240-360 mg BID cohorts where regressions began

efficacy.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
efficacy.note: PLX4720 regressed BRAF V600E xenografts and spared BRAF-wild-type cells; vemurafenib repeated this in A375, Colo829 and LOX.
efficacy.quote: In B-Raf(V600E)-dependent tumor xenograft models, orally dosed PLX4720 causes significant tumor growth delays, including tumor regressions, without evidence of toxicity.
efficacy.judgement: Strip opener. Vemurafenib itself was profiled in V600E melanoma xenografts in Yang 2010 (doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-10-0646), the models the FDA pharmacology review names.

efficacy.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
efficacy.note: Xenografts regressed; 26 of 32 V600E patients at the 960 mg BID extension cohort responded; phase 3 OS/PFS (vemurafenib), PFS (dabrafenib, encorafenib) followed.
efficacy.quote: Indeed, the Phase 1 clinical data revealed a remarkably high 81% response rate in metastatic melanoma patients treated at an oral dose of 960 mg twice daily.
efficacy.judgement: Same paper reports xenograft regression and the phase-1 response (NCT00405587; trial report Flaherty 2010, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1002011). The phase-1 primary endpoints were PK/safety; the 32-patient V600E extension cohort at the RP2D was the sponsor's efficacy gate, so endpoint_role is poc_gate. Response rate is a surrogate; the outcome trial BRIM-3 (co-primary OS and PFS) was positive, so outcome_tested is positive. Dabrafenib (BREAK-3, PFS) and encorafenib (COLUMBUS, PFS) repeated the class result in patient_trials. No member drug was flagged by the model and failed, so no neg. Sorafenib, which delayed melanoma xenografts and failed in unselected melanoma, is not a member and was trialled outside the V600-mutant population: set aside, not scored. Magnitude is direction_only: xenograft regression and RECIST response rate are different metrics.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft regression vs RECIST objective response rate

patient_trials.quote: Vemurafenib produced improved rates of overall and progression-free survival in patients with previously untreated melanoma with the BRAF V600E mutation.
Median progression-free survival was 5·1 months for dabrafenib and 2·7 months for dacarbazine, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0·30 (95% CI 0·18-0·51; p<0·0001).
Encorafenib plus binimetinib and encorafenib monotherapy showed favourable efficacy compared with vemurafenib.

efficacy.model: BRAF V600E vs wild-type cell-line panel (patient selection)
efficacy.note: Cell-line selectivity predicted who responds: 11 of 16 V600E patients but 0 of 5 BRAF-wild-type patients above 300 uM.h responded, and enrolment was restricted to BRAF-mutant tumours.
efficacy.quote: These data along with preclinical evidence of selectivity for BRAF-mutant cell lines strongly justified limiting all further enrollment to patients with BRAF-mutant tumors.
efficacy.confidence_note: Quote from the PMC author manuscript (PMC2948082): 'Ten patients with BRAF-mutant melanoma achieved ... partial responses ... and one patient had a complete response (CR); none of the patients with melanomas lacking BRAF mutations achieved PR.'
efficacy.reason: Xenograft regression and V600E-only rule both held
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction on the same system, kept on one track per the task's identity rule (same model, same cell-line panel; a different question). The panel's V600E-only sensitivity (Tsai 2008; Yang 2010: no activity in wild-type or non-V600 lines) became the enrolment rule for BRIM-2/3 and the label population; the 2013 Tafinlar label ties its wild-type limitation to 'in vitro experiments' on paradoxical activation, but no indication was granted on model data, so regulatory_reliance stays false.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: response by BRAF genotype: 11/16 V600E vs 0/5 wild-type at AUC0-24 >300 uM.h

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 23302800, epub 2013-01-09). Two primary human melanoma xenograft lines selected to vemurafenib resistance by continuous dosing.
efficacy.note: Vemurafenib-resistant xenografts became drug-dependent; a discontinuous (4-weeks-on/2-off) vemurafenib schedule forestalled lethal resistance. No patient test yet.
efficacy.short: Intermittent dosing forestalls resistance in xenografts
efficacy.quote: We further demonstrate that a discontinuous dosing strategy, which exploits the fitness disadvantage displayed by drug-resistant cells in the absence of the drug, forestalls the onset of lethal drug-resistant disease.
efficacy.judgement: Opened as its own track: a different system (resistant, drug-addicted xenografts) making a different prediction (a schedule prevents resistance) from the V600E-xenograft track. Prospective: S1320 was registered 18 months later to test it.

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: post-randomisation median PFS: 9.0 months continuous vs 5.5 months intermittent (105 vs 101 patients)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 33020646, epub 2020-10-05). NCT02196181 first posted 2014-07-21; no results posted on the registry as of 2026-11. P = 0.064 against a pre-specified two-sided alpha of 0.2.

patient_trials.quote: Continuous dosing yielded a statistically significant improvement in post-randomization progression-free survival compared with intermittent dosing (median 9.0 months versus 5.5 months, P = 0.064, pre-specified two-sided α = 0.2).

efficacy.note: SWOG S1320: intermittent dabrafenib+trametinib (3 weeks off, 5 on) shortened post-randomisation PFS, median 5.5 vs 9.0 months continuous; prediction reversed.
efficacy.quote: Therefore, contrary to the initial hypothesis, intermittent dosing did not improve progression-free survival in patients.
efficacy.population: BRAF V600-mutant, non-progressing after an 8-week continuous lead-in
efficacy.judgement: Placed in efficacy, not dose: the model's claim was a schedule-efficacy claim (longer control of resistance), the schedule was delivered exactly as randomised with no exposure target to reach, and the trial's primary endpoint (PFS) is what answered it; a derived dose entry would count the one failure twice. product_in_model false: the model used vemurafenib, the trial dabrafenib (a member) plus trametinib (not a member); both drugs were withheld in the intermittent arm, and the paper attributes the test to the BRAF-inhibitor drug-addiction hypothesis, so the contra is anchored on the class drug. Scored opposite: PFS moved against the prediction, not merely short of it.

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: primary endpoint PFS not improved by the intermittent schedule (medians not read)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 34853302). PFS medians not read; the abstract states the primary endpoint of PFS improvement was not met. NCT02583516 first posted 2015-10-22; no results posted.

patient_trials.quote: The trial did not meet its primary endpoint of progression free survival (PFS) improvement.

efficacy.note: Spanish phase 2 (NCT02583516): intermittent vemurafenib+cobimetinib missed its PFS primary; the model's own drug, same answer.
efficacy.short: Vemurafenib intermittent trial also missed PFS
efficacy.quote: Our results show that the antitumor activity of the experimental intermittent schedule of vemurafenib plus cobimetinib is not superior to the standard continuous schedule.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the contra with the model's own drug (vemurafenib) in patients; the paper itself sets the preclinical intermittent-dosing rationale against the result. Cobimetinib (non-member) was co-dosed, as in S1320.

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: median PFS 8.5 months intermittent vs 10.7 months continuous (HR 1.39); ORR 57% vs 77%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 38029480, epub 2023-11-24, print Eur J Cancer 2024). 79 patients; PFS HR 1.39 (95% CI 0.79-2.45, p = 0.255), underpowered but same direction as S1320. NCT03352947 first posted 2017-11-24; no results posted.

patient_trials.quote: With 19 months median follow-up, INT was inferior in all efficacy measures: median PFS 8.5 vs 10.7mo (HR 1.39, 95 %CI 0.79-2.45, p = 0.255)

efficacy.note: INTERIM (NCT03352947): intermittent dabrafenib+trametinib inferior on every efficacy measure, median PFS 8.5 vs 10.7 months; composite PFS+QoL primary.
efficacy.quote: INTERIM findings are consistent with other recent clinical trials reporting that intermittent dosing does not improve efficacy of BRAF+MEK inhibitors.
efficacy.reason: Three trials: intermittent dosing never beat continuous
efficacy.judgement: Third randomised test, third miss; the paper states the comparison with the preclinical rationale. Composite primary (PFS and QoL) treated as the primary; both components favoured continuous dosing.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via Europe PMC (PMC4259423). Oncotarget 5(20):9609, 2014.
efficacy.note: Gothenburg melanoma PDX programme: 23 of 26 biopsies engrafted with histology, mutations and expression matching the donor; built to guide treatment.
efficacy.short: Melanoma PDX built to guide treatment
efficacy.quote: Here tumor biopsies from patients with stage III and IV metastatic malignant melanoma were transplanted into immunocompromised mice to generate PDXes.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the patient-level PDX track at its first use; the first comparison is in the same paper.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of response to BRAF inhibitor, MEK inhibitor and the combination in one patient vs nine PDX
efficacy.confidence_note: Quote is the Figure 3 legend. n = 1 patient, treated in an unnamed BRAF/MEK-inhibitor trial; the PDX arms were run to mimic that trial after the patient's responses were in, so a retrodiction. Patient's own drugs not named in the sentences read.
efficacy.note: Case 2: nine PDX randomised to vemurafenib, trametinib or both reproduced the donor's responses to BRAF inhibitor, MEK inhibitor and combination.
efficacy.short: One patient's PDX matched her responses
efficacy.quote: The responses of Case 2 (patient M120521A) to BRAF inhibitors, MEK inhibitors or both were similar in the patient and the PDX model
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the PDX arms were designed to mimic a trial the patient had already been through. Patient-level because the question is whether this patient's tumour responds. PDX dosed with vemurafenib, a member.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.magnitude_basis: durability of BRAF-inhibitor benefit: patient PFS 16 weeks vs PDX no response on PLX4720, regression then relapse on combination
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read on PMC (PMC5726788), section 'Predictive Value of PDX for Response to Targeted Therapies'. Partial: the patient had a 70.6% partial response before relapsing at 16 weeks, which the PDX (no response to PLX4720) did not reproduce; the paper counts the early relapse as the prediction. PDX dosed with the tool analogue PLX4720, not vemurafenib.
efficacy.note: Wistar collection (459 PDX): pre-therapy PDX from a patient relapsing on vemurafenib at 16 weeks did not respond to BRAF inhibitor; progressed-patient PDX stayed resistant.
efficacy.short: Pre-therapy PDX reproduced early vemurafenib relapse
efficacy.quote: Tumors did not respond to BRAF inhibition, but regressed on BRAF/MEKi combination followed by relapse
efficacy.population: BRAF V600E melanoma relapsing on vemurafenib (one patient); 47 BRAFi/MEKi-progressed patients
efficacy.judgement: Kept on the one PDX track: same system (melanoma PDX) and same prediction (the donor's response) as Einarsdottir, a different institution. Retro with partial: resistance reproduced, the initial partial response not; a checker could read the missed initial response as contra. The 57 progressed-patient PDX were maintained on BRAFi or BRAFi+MEKi diet matching each patient's therapy and stayed resistant, a second concordance in the same paper.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.magnitude_basis: resistant vs sensitive by donor's prior BRAF-inhibitor progression: 4/4 progressed resistant, 3/3 naive sensitive
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via Europe PMC (PMC7054294; epub 2019-12-20, print Br J Cancer 2020). The patient comparison is made on PDX-derived cultures (PDXC) screened with vemurafenib and cobimetinib; the in-vivo PDX correlated with the cultures (vemurafenib rho = 0.98). Seven matched donors; no trial named.
efficacy.note: Eight BRAF-mutant PDX and their cultures: all four from patients progressed on BRAF inhibitor were vemurafenib-resistant, three treatment-naive responded; PDX vs culture rho 0.98.
efficacy.quote: Overall, PDXCs recapitulate the resistance to BRAF and MEK inhibitor therapy observed in the patient, and PDXCs from treatment-naive BRAF-mutant melanoma patients showed a marked response to BRAF and MEK inhibitor therapy.
efficacy.population: BRAF V600E/K metastatic melanoma, treatment-naive or progressed on BRAF/MEK inhibitors
efficacy.reason: PDX reproduce donors' BRAFi sensitivity/resistance after the fact
efficacy.judgement: Retro: every donor's BRAF-inhibitor outcome was known before the PDX/PDXC were screened. No prospective, PDX-guided treatment decision for a member drug has been reported, so the track never leaves retro.

safety.note: IND-enabling rat/dog toxicology (liver the target organ) preceded the Dec-2006 phase-1 start; no patient comparison yet.
safety.short: Rat/dog tox: liver, nothing on skin
safety.quote: The major target organ for toxicity in both rats and dogs appeared to be the liver.
safety.confidence_note: Proxy opener: the 2011 review describes the package; the first-in-human trial NCT00405587 was first posted 2006-11-30, so the package existed by then.
safety.judgement: Separate track from the xenografts: a different system answering a different question (tolerability), per the task's identity rule.

safety.note: Rat/dog skin showed no histological change at any dose, yet 31% of the 960 mg BID extension cohort developed keratoacanthoma-type cutaneous SCC.
safety.quote: Eight patients in the dose-escalation cohort (15%) and 10 patients in the extension cohort (31%) had cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas, with a total of 35 carcinomas.
safety.confidence_note: Patient quote from the PMC author manuscript (PMC3724529). Model side, Bollag 2010 manuscript: 'Importantly, no histological changes were observed in the skin in any animal at any dose or duration of treatment, contrasting to results observed with other RAF inhibitors.'
safety.judgement: A stated prediction (no skin change in 26-week rat and 13-week dog studies) contradicted on a harm the species' skin could have shown, so contra, magnitude opposite. Paired by me (Bollag 2010 is the model side); whether Bollag's published version also carries the 31% patient figure I could not confirm from the manuscript, so comparison_stated is false. Dated 2010 when both sides were public (Flaherty Aug 2010, Bollag Sept 2010).
safety.magnitude_basis: skin: no histological change in rat or dog at any dose vs cuSCC in 31% of patients at the MTD

safety.model: BRAF-wild-type / RAS-mutant cells and Kras-driven mice (paradoxical RAF activation)
safety.note: After the 2009 clinic reports, RAS-mutant cells and kinase-dead Braf/Kras mice showed BRAF-selective drugs drive CRAF-MEK-ERK and tumour growth, offered as the explanation of patient cuSCC.
safety.short: Paradoxical activation explains cuSCC, post hoc
safety.quote: Intriguingly, 10%–15% of patients treated with BRAF-selective drugs develop squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) (Flaherty et al., 2009; Schwartz et al., 2009).
safety.confidence_note: Quote from the PMC author manuscript (PMC2872605), discussion; the paper continues 'raising the intriguing possibility that the BRAF-selective drugs act as tumor promoters in premalignant skin cells harboring existing mutations in RAS'. Model drugs were PLX4720/885-A, not a member.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the cuSCC were reported at ASCO 2009 (Flaherty 2009; Schwartz 2009) before Heidorn (Cell, Jan 2010), Hatzivassiliou (doi:10.1038/nature08833) and Poulikakos (doi:10.1038/nature08902, both Feb 2010) published the dimer-transactivation model; Heidorn is cited because it alone names the patient SCC beside its data. Reproduced the direction of the human harm, so retro, not same; the source offers it as a possibility, so source_calls_it is unresolved. A third track: a different system (RAS-mutant, BRAF-wild-type cells) with a different prediction from the V600E xenografts and the tox package. model_filed true because the 2013 Tafinlar label (section 5.2) and the 2018 Braftovi review cite the in-vitro paradoxical activation; the 2011 vemurafenib NDA instead filed a post-hoc A431 xenograft (own track).
safety.magnitude_basis: RAF-inhibitor-driven growth of RAS-mutant cells/tumours vs 10-15% cuSCC incidence; no numeric prediction

safety.note: FDA's toxicity correlation table: cuSCC ~29% of patients, rat and dog columns blank; genotoxicity negative yet cuSCC developed rapidly in the clinic.
safety.quote: Nevertheless, in the clinical studies vemurafenib dosing was associated with the rapid development and growth of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
safety.confidence_note: Pharmacology review pp.105-106: 'Correlation with Clinical Toxicity' table lists Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma ~29% in humans, 'Modeled in Athymic Mice', with the rat and dog cells empty.
safety.judgement: Regulator-stated restatement of the 2010 miss, kept as a strengthening entry. Dabrafenib (cuSCC 7% in BREAK-3, 11% across trials, 2013 label) and encorafenib (16.7% vemurafenib vs 7.8% encorafenib arm in COLUMBUS, 2018 review) carried the same class harm.
safety.magnitude_basis: cuSCC ~29% in patients vs no finding in rat or dog toxicology

safety.model: A431 cutaneous SCC xenograft in athymic mice (sponsor, post hoc)
safety.note: Built after the clinical finding: vemurafenib dose-dependently accelerated SCC xenograft growth, but a second V600E inhibitor did not and pMEK/pMAPK staining did not rise; FDA: mechanism undetermined.
safety.short: Post-hoc SCC xenograft grew faster, mechanism unclear
safety.quote: Experiments in which nude mice implanted with SCC cells were administered vemurafenib showed a dose-dependent increase in tumor growth.
safety.confidence_note: Review executive summary and pp.104-105 ('To investigate potential mechanisms for this finding, the sponsor conducted xenograft experiments with human SCC cells in nude mice'); study dates are not given in the text I grepped, so model_first_use_year is the review year.
safety.reason: Post-hoc xenograft reproduced growth; mechanism unresolved
safety.judgement: Own track: a different system (RAS-wild-type A431 SCC xenograft) from the paradox model, run by the sponsor after the clinic knew the answer, so retrodiction. It reproduced the growth acceleration (retro) but the review calls the mechanism off-target and undetermined, pointing away from paradoxical MEK activation (no pMEK/pMAPK increase; RO5212054 inactive), so source_calls_it is unresolved. This is the model the vemurafenib NDA filed for cuSCC.
safety.magnitude_basis: dose-dependent SCC xenograft growth acceleration vs clinical cuSCC promotion

safety.model: HRAS Q61L keratinocytes and DMBA/TPA mouse skin (paradoxical RAF activation)
safety.note: First prospective test: 60% (21/35) of patient cuSCC/keratoacanthomas carried RAS mutations (HRAS Q61L); PLX4720 accelerated HRAS-mutant mouse lesions and a MEK inhibitor blocked it.
safety.short: Patient cuSCC are RAS-mutant, as predicted
safety.quote: The molecular mechanism is consistent with the paradoxical activation of MAPK signaling and leads to accelerated growth of these lesions.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract verbatim; full text read via the PMC author manuscript (PMC3724537). Patient side: 'Thus, 60% (21 of 35) of the specimens harbored RAS mutations, the most prevalent being HRAS Q61L.'
safety.judgement: The 2010 model's forward prediction (lesions arise from RAS-primed keratinocytes; MEK inhibition should block) tested in patient lesions from NCT00405587, NCT00949702, NCT01001299 and NCT01006980 and in the HRAS Q61L mouse, with vemurafenib in the cell lines and PLX4720 in mice: same, a fresh prospective entry after the retrodiction (decision 10). Oberholzer 2011 (doi:10.1200/JCO.2011.36.7680, epub 2011-11-07) found RAS mutations enriched (21% vs 3%) earlier but pooled vemurafenib with sorafenib (not a member) across 19 patients, so the entry is dated on the vemurafenib-only series. registry_date is the earliest results posting among the four trials (NCT01006980).
safety.magnitude_basis: RAS-mutant fraction of patient lesions (60%) vs the model's qualitative RAS-primed prediction

safety.model: HRAS Q61L keratinocytes and DMBA/TPA mouse skin (paradoxical RAF activation)
safety.note: The model's MEK-block prediction held in phase 3: dabrafenib plus trametinib cut cuSCC to 2% from 9% on dabrafenib alone (COMBI-d).
safety.quote: The rate of cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma was lower in the dabrafenib-trametinib group than in the dabrafenib-only group (2% vs. 9%)
safety.confidence_note: Verbatim first clause of a 43-word abstract sentence (the remainder concerns pyrexia). Paired by me; mouse MEK inhibitor was PD184352, not trametinib.
safety.reason: RAS-mutant skin model held; MEK block cut cuSCC
safety.judgement: Paired comparison: Su 2012's mouse (MEK inhibitor suppressed PLX4720-accelerated tumour development by 91%) against COMBI-d (NCT01584648, results posted 2014-08-15; dabrafenib is a member), a 78% relative reduction, so within_2x. The earlier phase 1/2 signal (Flaherty 2012, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1210093: 7% vs 19%, P=0.09, NCT01072175 results 2013-11-21) was non-significant, so the entry is dated on the phase 3. The 2018 Braftovi review states the same reliance ('Coadministration with MEK inhibitors has been shown to reduce the incidence of these hyperproliferative lesions by blocking paradoxical MAPK activation'): cuSCC 2.6% combination, 7.8% encorafenib, 16.7% vemurafenib.
safety.magnitude_basis: relative reduction of cuSCC by MEK co-inhibition: 91% in DMBA/TPA/PLX4720 mice vs 78% (9% to 2%) in COMBI-d
